I raised the document in my hand and said, ‘Messenger of Allah, this is your document.’ The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, ‘A day of fulfillment and kindness. Bring him near.’ He said: Then I accepted Islam.
Then I mentioned something I wanted to ask the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about.
Ibn Shihab said: He had only asked him about the lost animals and something he had done to him when they were in that situation. I mentioned nothing except that I said, ‘Messenger of Allah, lost animals come to my watering troughs ...’”
H-7478-1012-RA-WOMAN-SON:p1:
Abu al-Hasan ‘Ali ibn Ahmad ibn ‘Abdan informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn ‘Ubayd al-Saffar informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn Yahya al-Hulwani and Muhammad ibn al-Fadl ibn Jabir informed us, both saying: Muhammad ibn ‘Imran ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Zakariyya ibn Abi Za’idah narrated to us.

(H) Abu al-Husayn ibn Bishran al-‘Adl also informed us in Baghdad—and this is his wording—saying: Abu al-Hasan ‘Ali ibn Muhammad al-Misri informed us, saying: ‘Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Maryam narrated to us, saying: Asad ibn Musa narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Zakariyya ibn Abi Za’idah narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla narrated to us, saying: ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Asbahani narrated to us, saying: I heard ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla relate from Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, who said:

“I set out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ from Makkah. We came to a clan of the Arabs, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw a house set apart and headed toward it. When we dismounted, there was no one inside but a woman. She said, ‘Servant of Allah, I am only a woman, and there is no one with me. If you want hospitality, you should go to the chief of the clan.’ He did not answer her. This was in the evening. Then her son came, driving some she-goats. She said to him, ‘My son, take these goats and the knife to these two men and tell them: “My mother says to you, slaughter this, eat, and feed us.”’ When he came, the Prophet ﷺ said to him
H-7478-1013-RA-WOMAN-IDENTITY:p1: I say: Although this account is shorter than the account of Umm Ma‘bad that we have related, and adds details in some parts, it is close to it, and it seems likely that they are one and the same. Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar mentioned something in the account of Umm Ma‘bad that indicates that this woman and she were one and the same. Allah knows best.
H-7478-1013-RA-WOMAN-SON:p1:
“Take the knife and bring me the cup.” He said, “They have been left without a male, and they have no milk.” He said, “Go.” So he went and brought a cup. The Prophet ﷺ stroked her udder, then milked her until he had filled the cup. Then he said, “Take it to your mother.” She drank until she was satisfied. Then he brought the cup back, and he said:

“Take this one and bring me another.” He did so with it in the same way. Then he gave Abu Bakr a drink. Then he brought another, and he did the same with it. Then the Prophet ﷺ drank.”

He said: We spent the night there, then set out. She used to call him “the Blessed One,” and her flock grew until she drove a herd to Madinah. Abu Bakr al-Siddiq passed by, and her son saw him and recognized him. He said, “Mother, this is the man who was with the Blessed One.” She went to him and said, “Servant of Allah, who was the man with you?” He said, “Do you know who he was?” She said, “No.” He said, “He was the Prophet ﷺ.” She said, “Then take me to him.” He took her to him, and he fed her and gave her something. Ibn ‘Abdan adds in his version: She said, “Show me where he is.” She went with me and brought him some dried yogurt and other Bedouin goods. He clothed her and gave her something. I believe he said, ‘She accepted Islam.’”
H-7478-1014-RA-UMM-ISHaq:p1: Abu ‘Abdullah al-Hafiz informed us, saying: Abu al-‘Abbas Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub told us, saying: Ahmad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar told us, saying: Yunus ibn Bukayr told us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: “The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stopped at Umm Ma‘bad’s tent. She was the one about whom the jinn sang at the upper part of Makkah. Her name was ‘Atikah bint Khalid ibn Munqidh ibn Rabi‘ah ibn Asram. They wanted hospitality, but she said, ‘By Allah, we have no food, no milch animal, and no sheep except a ewe that is not producing milk.’ The Messenger of Allah ﷺ called for one of her sheep, rubbed its udder with his hand, prayed to Allah, and milked it into a vessel until it foamed. He said, ‘Drink, Umm Ma‘bad.’ She said, ‘You drink; you have more right to it.’ He gave it back to her, and she drank. Then he called for another ewe that was not producing milk, did the same, and drank. Then he called for another such ewe, did the same, and gave the guide a drink. Then he called for another such ewe, did the same, and gave ‘Amir a drink. Then they set off. Quraysh pursued the Messenger of Allah ﷺ until they reached Umm Ma‘bad and asked her about him. They said, ‘Did you see Muhammad, whose appearance is such-and-such?’ They described him to her, but she said, ‘I don’t know what you mean. A man who milked an ewe that was not producing milk stayed with me.’ Quraysh said, ‘That is the one we are looking for.’”
H-7478-1014-RA-UMM-RECONCILE:p1: I say: It is possible that the first incident was the one involving the tent being taken down, as we related in the hadith of Umm Ma‘bad. Then her son returned with some she-goats, as we related in the hadith of Ibn Abi Layla. Then
H-7478-1015-RA-UMM-RECONCILE:p1: when her husband came, she described him to him. Allah knows best.
H-7478-1027-RA-BADR:p1: Abu ‘Amr al-Adīb informed us, saying: Abu Bakr al-Ismā‘īlī informed us, saying: I heard Abu Khalīfah say: I heard Ibn ‘Ā’ishah say: “When he arrived…”
H-7478-1028-RA-BADR:p1: in Madinah, the women and children began to say: “The full moon has risen over us from the passes of al-Wadā‘; gratitude is incumbent upon us whenever someone calls upon Allah.”
H-7478-1030-RA-ZUBAYR-ARBOR:p1: ‘Ali ibn Ahmad ibn ‘Abdan reported to us: Ahmad ibn ‘Ubayd al-Saffar reported to us: Khalaf ibn ‘Amr al-‘Ukbari narrated to us: Sa‘id ibn Mansur narrated to us: ‘Attaf ibn Khalid narrated to us: Siddi q ibn Musa narrated to us, from ‘Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ arrived in Madinah. His riding camel knelt with him between the house of Ja‘far ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Ali and the house of al-Hasan ibn Zayd. People came to him and said, “O Messenger of Allah, [come to] the lodging.” His camel set off with him, and he said, “Leave her, for she has been commanded.” Then she went on with him until she came to the place of the pulpit and knelt. Then she made her way through the people. There was an arbor there that they watered, maintained, and rested in to keep cool. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ dismounted from his camel and took shelter in the shade, settling there. Abu Ayyub came to him and said, “O Messenger of Allah, my house is the closest of the houses to you, so move your belongings to me.” He said, “Yes.” Abu Ayyub took his belongings to his house. Then a man came and asked, “O Messenger of Allah, where will you stay?” He said, “A man is with his belongings wherever they may be.” The Messenger of Allah ﷺ remained in the arbor for twelve nights, until the mosque was built.”
H-7478-1032-RA-DATE-ZUHRI:p1: Abu al-Husayn ibn Bishran al-‘Adl informed us in Baghdad. He said: Abu ‘Amr ibn al-Sammak informed us. He said: Hanbal ibn Ishaq told us. He said: Abu ‘Abdullah Ahmad ibn Hanbal told me. He said: Hajjaj ibn Muhammad told us. He said: Layth ibn Sa‘d told us. He said: ‘Uqayl told me, from Ibn Shihab, who said: “There were three months, or close to that, between the Night of al-‘Aqabah and the Messenger of Allah’s ﷺ migration. The Ansar pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the Night of al-‘Aqabah in Dhu al-Hijjah. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ arrived in Madinah in Rabi‘ al-Awwal, and he died in Rabi‘ al-Awwal, ten years after completing his migration from Makkah to Madinah.”
H-7478-1061-RA-MOSQUE-HAMMAD:p1:
Abu ‘Ali al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Rudhbari reported to us: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Bakr ibn Dasah al-Tammar reported to us in Basra: Abu Dawud al-Sijistani narrated to us:
Musa ibn Isma‘il narrated to us: Hammad—namely, ibn Salamah—narrated to us, from Abu al-Tayyah, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: “The site of the mosque was an enclosure belonging to the Banu al-Najjar. It contained cultivated land, palm trees, and the graves of polytheists. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, ‘Name your price for it.’ They replied, ‘We want no payment.’ He cut down the palm trees, leveled the cultivated land, and exhumed the graves of the polytheists.” He then related the hadith. He also said:
“So forgive, [and] grant victory in its place.”
Musa said: ‘Abd al-Warith narrated to us something similar. ‘Abd al-Warith used to say, “ruins.” ‘Abd al-Warith claimed that he had given this hadith to Hammad.
H-7478-1061-RA-MOSQUE-IBNUMAR:p1: Abu ‘Ali [al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Rudhbarī] informed us. He said: Abu Bakr
H-7478-1062-RA-MOSQUE-IBNUMAR:p1: ibn Dasah said: Abu Dawud narrated to us: Mujahid ibn Musa narrated to us: Ya‘qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to us: My father narrated to us, from Salih, who said: Nafi‘ narrated to us that ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar informed him: “In the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, the mosque was built of mud bricks, its roof was made of palm fronds, and its supports were palm trunks. Abu Bakr made no additions to it. ‘Umar enlarged it and rebuilt it on the same plan as it had in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, using mud bricks and palm fronds; he replaced its supports with wooden ones. ‘Uthman changed it, enlarged it considerably, built its walls of carved stone and mortar, made its supports of carved stone, and gave it a teak roof.” Al-Bukhari narrated it in al-Sahih, from ‘Ali ibn al-Madini, from Ya‘qub.
H-7478-1063-RA-MOSQUE-UBADA:p1: Abu al-Husayn ibn Bishran reported to us: Abu al-Hasan al-Basri reported to us: Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Hammad narrated to us: Abu Salamah al-Minqarī narrated to us: Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Abu Sinan, from Ya‘la ibn Shaddad ibn Aws, from ‘Ubadah, that the Ansar gathered some money and brought it to the Prophet ﷺ. They said, “Messenger of Allah, build this mosque for us and adorn it. How long must we pray beneath these palm fronds?” He replied, “I have no desire to do otherwise than my brother Moses; a shelter like the shelter of Moses.”
H-7478-1066-RA-MOSQUE-UMAR:p1:
Abu al-Hasan ‘Ali ibn Muhammad al-Muqri’ reported to us: al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Ishaq reported to us: Yusuf ibn Ya‘qub narrated to us: ‘Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Abu al-Ahwas narrated to us, from Simak ibn Harb, from Sayyar ibn al-Ma‘rur, who said:
“‘Umar ibn al-Khattab addressed us and said, ‘People, this mosque was built by the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, with us, the Emigrants and the Ansar, alongside him. Pray in it. If any of you cannot find a place, let him prostrate on his brother’s back.’”
H-7478-1067-RA-AMMAR-KHALID-A:p1:
Abu ‘Abdullah al-Hafiz informed us, saying: Abu ‘Amr ibn Abi Ja‘far informed me, saying: Abu al-Qasim al-Baghawi narrated to us, saying: Abu Kamil al-Jahdari narrated to us, saying:
‘Abd al-‘Aziz ibn al-Mukhtar narrated to us, saying: Khalid al-Hadhdha’ narrated to us, from ‘Ikrimah, that Ibn ‘Abbas said to him and to his son ‘Ali: “Go to Abu Sa‘id and listen to his hadith.” ‘Ikrimah said: “We went, and there he was in a garden of his, tending it. When he saw us, he took his cloak, wrapped it around himself while sitting, and began telling us hadith until he came to the account of the building of the mosque. He said: ‘We used to carry one mud brick at a time, while ‘Ammar carried two at a time. The Prophet ﷺ saw him, began brushing the dust off him, and said:
“Alas for ‘Ammar! The rebellious faction will kill him. He calls them to Paradise, while they call him to the Fire.”’ He said:
‘“‘Ammar used to say: I seek refuge in Allah from trials.”’”
Al-Bukhari related it in his Sahih from Musaddad, from ‘Abd al-‘Aziz, but did not mention the words, “The rebellious faction will kill him.”
H-7478-1068-RA-AMMAR-KHALID-B:p1: Abu ‘Amr Muhammad ibn ‘Abdullah al-Bistami informed us, saying: Abu Bakr al-Isma‘ili informed us, saying: ‘Imran ibn Musa informed me, saying: Wahb ibn Baqiyyah narrated to us, saying: Khalid—that is, Ibn ‘Abdullah al-Wasiti—informed us. Ibn ‘Abd al-Karim also narrated to us, saying: Ishaq ibn Shahin informed us, saying: Khalid narrated to us, from ‘Ikrimah, that Ibn ‘Abbas said to me and to ‘Ali ibn ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Abbas: “Go to Abu Sa‘id and listen to his hadith.” We went to him and found him in a garden of his. When he saw us, he came over, took his cloak, then sat down and began telling us hadith until he came to the account of the building of the mosque. He said: “We used to carry one mud brick at a time, while ‘Ammar carried two at a time. The Prophet ﷺ saw him and began brushing the dust from ‘Ammar’s head, saying: ‘O ‘Ammar, why don’t you carry them as your companions do?’ He said: ‘I seek the reward from Allah.’ He then began brushing the dust off him and saying: ‘Alas for ‘Ammar! The rebellious faction will kill him. He calls them to Paradise, while they call him to the Fire.’ ‘Ammar said: ‘I seek refuge in the Most Merciful from trials.’”
H-7478-1069-RA-AMMAR-CRITIC-A:p1: It seems he omitted it only because ‘Ikrimah’s account from Abu Sa‘id differed from that of Abu Nadrah from Abu Sa‘id on this point.
H-7478-1070-RA-AMMAR-CRITIC-B:p1: What is reported from Abu Nadrata, from Abu Sa‘id al-Khudri, in this narration clarifies what was heard from others about this hadith. It also reports carrying one or two bricks, as ‘Ikrimah reported. It seems that he mentioned the Trench while the two of them were there, according to Abu Nadrata’s narration; or perhaps he said this when the mosque was being built and said it again on the day of the Trench. Allah knows best.
H-7478-1072-RA-AMMAR-SIFFIN-MEMORY:p1: Abu ‘Abdullah al-Hafiz narrated to us: Abu Zakariya al-‘Anbari narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Salam narrated to us: Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Hanzali narrated to us: ‘Ata
H-7478-1073-RA-AMMAR-SIFFIN-MEMORY:p1: ibn Muslim al-Halabi said: I heard al-A‘mash say: Abu ‘Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami said, “We witnessed Siffin. Whenever we agreed to a truce, these men would enter the camp of those men, and those men would enter the camp of these men. I saw four men riding together: Mu‘awiyah ibn Abi Sufyan, Abu al-A‘war al-Sulami, ‘Amr ibn al-‘As, and his son. I heard ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Amr say to his father, ‘We have killed this man, although the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said what he said about him.’ He asked, ‘Which man?’ He replied, ‘‘Ammar ibn Yasir. Do you not remember the day the Messenger of Allah ﷺ built the mosque? We carried one brick at a time, while ‘Ammar carried two at a time. He passed by the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who said, “You are carrying two bricks at a time, and you are covered in dust. The rebellious faction will kill you, and you are one of the people of Paradise.”’ ‘Amr went in to see Mu‘awiyah and said, ‘We have killed this man, although the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said what he said about him.’ He replied, ‘Be quiet! By Allah, you are still floundering in your own urine! Did we kill him? ‘Ali and his companions killed him; they brought him here and threw him down among us.’”
H-7478-2236-CRIT-BADRTABUK:p1:
Abu Nasr ibn Qatadah reported to us, saying: Abu ‘Amr ibn Matar reported to us. He said: I heard Abu Khalifah say: I heard Ibn ‘Aishah say:
When the Prophet ﷺ arrived in Madinah, the women, children, and young girls began singing:
“The full moon has risen over us
From the passes of al-Wada‘.
Gratitude is incumbent upon us
Whenever anyone calls upon Allah.”
I say: Our scholars mention this when he arrived in Madinah from Makkah. We have mentioned it in that context, not when he arrived in Madinah via the passes of al-Wada‘ on his return from Tabuk. Allah knows best; we have mentioned it here as well.
H-7478-996-RA-AISHA-LONG:p1:
He would hear any plan they devised against them and memorize it, then bring them news of it when darkness fell. ‘Amir ibn Fuhayrah, Abu Bakr’s freedman, grazed a flock of sheep for them. After an hour of the night had passed, he brought the sheep to them, and they spent the night drinking their milk and warming themselves with heated stones, until ‘Amir ibn Fuhayrah called them at the break of dawn. He did this each night during those three nights.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ and Abu Bakr hired a man from Banu al-Dayl, of Banu ‘Abd ibn ‘Adiy, as a skilled guide. A skilled guide is one who is adept at finding the way. He had made an alliance with the family of al-‘As ibn Wa’il and followed the religion of Quraysh’s unbelievers, but they trusted him. They handed him their two mounts and arranged to meet him at the Cave of Thawr. He brought their mounts to them on the morning of the third night. They set out, and ‘Amir ibn Fuhayrah and the Dalite guide went with them, taking the coastal route.”
H-7478-997-RA-IBNSIRIN-CAVE:p1:
Abu ‘Abdullah al-Hafiz dictated to us, saying: Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Musa ibn al-Hasan ibn ‘Abbad informed us, saying: ‘Affan ibn Muslim narrated to us, saying: al-Sari ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Sirin narrated to us, saying:
“Some men were mentioned during ‘Umar’s time, and it seemed they were giving ‘Umar precedence over Abu Bakr. When ‘Umar heard of this, he said, ‘By Allah, one night of Abu Bakr’s is better than all of ‘Umar’s family, and one day of Abu Bakr’s is better than all of ‘Umar’s family. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ set out one night for the cave, accompanied by Abu Bakr. Abu Bakr would walk for a while ahead of him and then for a while behind him, until the Messenger of Allah ﷺ noticed. He said, “Abu Bakr, why do you walk for a while ahead of me and then for a while behind me?” He replied, “Messenger of Allah, I think of the pursuers, so I walk behind you; then I think of those lying in wait, so I walk ahead of you.” He said, “Abu Bakr, if something were to happen, would you want it to happen to you rather than to me?” He replied, “Yes. By the One who sent you with the truth, whenever calamity threatened, I would want it to befall me and not you.”
“When we reached the cave, Abu Bakr said, ‘Stay here, Messenger of Allah, until I inspect the cave for you.’ He went in and inspected it. When he reached the upper part, he remembered that he had not checked the hole. He said, ‘Stay here, Messenger of Allah, until I inspect the hole.’ He went in and checked it, then said, ‘Come down, Messenger of Allah.’ He came down, and ‘Umar said, ‘By the One in whose hand is my soul, that night is better than all of ‘Umar’s family.’”
H-7478-998-RA-DABBA-CAVE:p1: …Ja‘far, while I was listening. He said: ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Ibrahim al-Rasibi told us; he said: Furat ibn al-Sa’ib narrated to me from Maymun ibn Mihran, from Dabba ibn Mihsan al-‘Anazi, from ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab, in an account he related. ‘Umar said: “By Allah, one night and one day of Abu Bakr’s are better than ‘Umar’s whole lifetime. Would you like me to tell you about his night and his day?” I said, “Yes, Commander of the Faithful.” He said: “As for his night, when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ left Makkah, fleeing its people, he went out at night, and Abu Bakr followed him. He would walk sometimes ahead of him, sometimes behind him, sometimes to his right, and sometimes to his left. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him, ‘What is this, Abu Bakr? I don’t usually see you behave like this.’ He replied, ‘Messenger of Allah, I think of those lying in wait, so I go ahead of you; then I think of those pursuing us, so I go behind you. At times I go to your right and at times to your left. I cannot feel safe for you.’ The Messenger of Allah ﷺ walked that night on the tips of his toes until his feet were sore. When Abu Bakr saw that his feet were sore, he carried him on his shoulders and hurried with him until he reached the mouth of the cave. He set him down, then said, ‘By the One who sent you with the truth, you will not enter it until I have entered it first. If there is anything inside, it will harm me before you.’ He went in and saw nothing, then carried him in. There was a hole in the cave containing snakes and vipers. Abu Bakr feared that something might come out and harm the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, so he plugged it with his foot. The snakes and vipers began striking and biting him, and his tears streamed down as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him, ‘Abu Bakr, do not grieve; Allah is with us.’ Allah sent down His tranquility upon Abu Bakr. This was his night.”
H-930-761-JUDGMENT:p1: This is a good chain of transmission, and it is among the best reports narrated about the spider weaving its web at the mouth of the cave. This was part of Allah’s protection of His Messenger ﷺ.
H-930-761-SPIDER:p1:
He said: One night in Makkah, Quraysh deliberated. Some of them said, “When morning comes, bind him securely”—meaning the Prophet ﷺ. Others said, “Rather, kill him.” Still others said, “Rather, drive him out.”

Allah informed His Prophet ﷺ of this. That night, ‘Ali lay in the Prophet’s ﷺ bed, while the Prophet ﷺ went out and reached the cave. The polytheists spent the night keeping watch over ‘Ali, thinking he was the Prophet ﷺ.

When morning came, they rushed at him. But when they saw ‘Ali, Allah thwarted their plot. They said, “Where is your companion?” He replied, “I do not know.”

They followed his trail. When they reached the mountain, they lost track of it. They climbed the mountain and passed by the cave. Seeing a spider’s web across its entrance, they said, “If anyone had entered here, there would not be a spider’s web at its entrance.” He remained there for three nights.
H-9783-1007-ALI-A:p1: ‘Ali ibn Abi Talib remained in Makkah for three nights and their days, until he had returned to the people the trusts that had been with him on behalf of the Messenger of Allah. When he had finished, he caught up with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and stayed with him at Kulthum ibn Hadm’s home. ‘Ali used to say: “His stay at Quba was only for a night or two with a Muslim woman who had no husband.” He also used to say: “I stayed at Quba with a Muslim woman who had no husband. I saw someone come to her in the middle of the night and knock on her door. She would go out to him, and he would give her something he had with him. I became suspicious about what was going on, so I said to her, ‘O servant of Allah, who is this man who knocks on your door every night, and you go out to him and he gives you something, though I do not know what it is? You are a Muslim woman with no husband!’ She said, ‘This is Sahl ibn Hunayf ibn Wahib. He knows that I am a woman with no one to help me. When evening comes, he goes and smashes the idols of his people, then brings them to me and says, “Use this for firewood.”’ ‘Ali ibn—
H-9783-1008-ALI-B:p1: Abu Talib used to relate this account of Sahl ibn Hunayf after Sahl died in his home in Iraq. Ibn Humayd told us: Salamah told us: Muhammad ibn Ishaq told me: ‘Ali ibn Hind ibn Sa‘d ibn Sahl ibn Hunayf told me this account, from ‘Ali ibn Abi Talib.
H-9783-1022-FIRST-DEATHS:p1:
Abu Ja‘far said: He ﷺ himself, together with his Companions from among the Emigrants and the Helpers, undertook the building of his mosque.

In this year, the mosque at Quba was built.

The first Muslim to die after his arrival in Madinah, according to what has been reported, was the owner of his lodging, Kulthum ibn al-Hidm. He lived only a short time after his arrival before he died.

Then, in the year of his arrival, As‘ad ibn Zurarah, Abu Umamah, died. He died before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had finished building his mosque, from quinsy and choking. Ibn Humayd reported to us: Salamah reported to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: ‘Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr reported to me, from Yahya ibn ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman, [that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “How ill-timed was the death of Abu Umamah! The Jews and the Arab hypocrites say: ‘If Muhammad were a prophet, his companion would not have died.’ I have no power over anything from Allah for myself or my companion.”]
H-9783-1025-FAMILY:p1:
In this year, the Prophet ﷺ sent Zayd ibn Harithah and Abu Rafi‘ to bring his daughters and his wife Sawdah bint Zam‘ah from Makkah to Madinah.
When, according to the report, ‘Abdullah ibn Urayqit returned to Makkah, he told ‘Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr where his father, Abu Bakr, was. ‘Abdullah set out with his father’s family to join him. Talhah ibn ‘Ubaydullah accompanied them, along with Umm Ruman, ‘Aishah’s mother, and ‘Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr, until they arrived in Madinah.
H-97932-80-DISTINCTION:p1: The assessments of the spider’s web as good by the two hadith scholars Ibn Kathir and Ibn Hajar apply only to the spider’s web. As far as I know, no one has authenticated the account of two doves laying eggs in the cave. Allah knows best.
H-9862-287-ISHAQ-EARLY-ADHAN-01:p1: Yunus narrated to us, from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Utbah, from ‘Amr ibn Murrah, from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, from Mu‘adh ibn Jabal, who said: “Prayer was prescribed in three stages, and fasting was prescribed in three stages. As for the stages of prayer: when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ arrived in Madinah, he prayed toward Jerusalem for seventeen months. Then Allah, Mighty and Exalted, turned him toward the qiblah. That was one stage. They were on the verge of using a bell when prayer time came, and then ‘Abdullah ibn Zayd al-Ansari came…”
H-9862-81-ISHAQ-EARLY-SALMAN-01:p1: Ahmad told us: Yunus ibn Bukayr told us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, who said: ‘Asim ibn ‘Umar ibn Qatadah told me, from Mahmud ibn Labid, from ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Abbas, who said: Salman al-Farisi told me: “I was a Persian from the people of Isfahan, from a village called Jayy. My father was the landowner of his estate, and he loved me very dearly, more than anything he possessed, whether wealth or children. His love for me grew so strong that he kept me confined in the house like a girl. I devoted myself to the Magian religion until I became the caretaker of the fire they kept burning, never letting it go out for even an hour. I remained that way, knowing nothing of people’s affairs except what concerned me, until my father began building a structure. He had an estate where some work was being done, so he called me and said, ‘My son, as you can see, this building has kept me busy and away from my estate. I need to inspect it. Go there and tell them to do such-and-such, and do not linger, for if you delay, you will distract me from everything else.’ I set out for his estate and passed by a Christian church. I heard their voices inside, so I said, ‘What is that?’ They said, ‘These Christians are praying.’ I went in to look, and what I saw of their way of worship impressed me. By Allah, I stayed with them until sunset. My father sent people out in every direction to look for me, and I reached him only when evening had come. I had not gone to the estate. He said, ‘My son, where were you? Did I not tell you?’ I said, ‘Father…’”
H-9862-84-ISHAQ-EARLY-SALMAN-04:p1: “And he does not eat from charity. If you can make your way to that land, do so, for his time is near.” After we buried him, I stayed on in the best of circumstances, until some Arab traders from Kalb passed by. I said to them, ‘Will you take me with you to the land of the Arabs? I will give you these sheep and my cows.’ They said, ‘Yes.’ So I gave them to them, and they took me along. But when they brought me to Wadi al-Qura, they wronged me and sold me as a slave to a Jewish man there. By Allah, when I saw the palm trees, I hoped that this was the land my companion had described to me. But I was not sure until a man from Banu Qurayzah, one of the Jews of Wadi al-Qura, came and bought me from my former owner. He took me away and brought me to Madinah. By Allah, as soon as I saw it, I recognized the description. I remained in slavery with my owner, while Allah ﷿ sent His Messenger ﷺ in Makkah. I heard nothing about him while I was a slave, until the Messenger of Allah ﷺ arrived at Quba. I was working for my owner on one of his palm trees when, by Allah, a cousin of his came and said, ‘So-and-so, may Allah destroy Banu Qaylah! By Allah, they are gathered in Quba right now around a man who has come from Makkah and claims to be a prophet.’ By Allah, when I heard this, I began to tremble, so much so that I thought I would fall on my owner. I climbed down and said, ‘What is this news? What is it?’ My master raised his hand and struck me hard, saying, ‘What is this to you? Get back to your work!’ I said, ‘Nothing. I just heard some news and wanted to know about it.’ When evening came, I had some food, so I carried it and went to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who was at Quba. I said, ‘I have heard that you are a righteous man, and that you have companions with you who are strangers here. I had some food for charity, and I thought you were the most deserving of it in this land. Here it is; eat from it.’ The Messenger of Allah ﷺ held back his hand and said to his Companions, ‘Eat,’ but he did not eat. I said to myself, ‘This is one of the traits my companion described to me.’ Then I returned. The Messenger of Allah moved...
H-9898-138-prep-1:p1: Al-Ansari Khalid ibn Zayd ibn Kulayb took hold of his baggage, and As‘ad ibn Zurarah came and took hold of the reins of his she-camel. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ asked about the mirbad. Mu‘adh ibn ‘Afra’ said, “It belongs to two orphan boys, and I will compensate them for it.” The Messenger of Allah ﷺ summoned the two boys and bargained with them for the mirbad, intending to make it a mosque. They said, “Rather, we give it to you as a gift.” But the Messenger of Allah ﷺ refused to accept their gift until he had bought it from them. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ left the mosque, they said, “Messenger of Allah, a man stays with the place where he has left his baggage.” So he stayed with Abu [Ayyub] al-Ansari, whose house was among Banu Ghanm ibn al-Najjar.
H-9898-138-prep-2:p1:
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the Muslims began building the mosque. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ carried bricks with them, saying:

“This is the carrier, not the carrier of Khaybar … This is more righteous [for our Lord] and purer.

O Allah, goodness is the goodness of the Hereafter … so forgive the Helpers and the Emigrants.”

‘Ammar ibn Yasir was short and curly-haired. He was carrying bricks, and dust had covered his chest. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: “Son of Sumayyah, the transgressing party will kill you!” Talq ibn ‘Ali arrived to join the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and helped the Muslims build the mosque. The Prophet ﷺ would say: “Bring the clay close to al-Yamami, for he is one of the best of you at handling it.” As‘ad ibn … died.
H-9898-140-prep-2:p1:
The Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ suffered a severe fever. ‘Aishah went in to Abu Bakr while he was saying:
“Everyone wakes among his family ... yet death is nearer than his sandal strap.”
Then she went in to ‘Amir ibn Fuhayrah while he was saying:
H-9898-141-prep-1:p1:
“Everyone is defended by his own strength ... the bull protects its hide with its horns.”
Then she went in to Bilal while he was saying:
“Would that I knew whether I would spend a night in a valley, with izkhir and jalil all around me;
And whether I would one day reach the waters of Majannah, and whether Shamah and Tufayl would appear to me.”
Bilal used to say: “O Allah, curse ‘Utbah ibn Rabi‘ah, Shaybah ibn Rabi‘ah, Abu Sufyan ibn Harb, and Abu Jahl ibn Hisham, just as they drove us out of Makkah.” ‘Aishah told the Prophet ﷺ what she had seen of their fever. The Prophet ﷺ said: “O Allah, make Madinah beloved to us as You made Makkah beloved to us, bless it for us as You blessed Makkah for us, bless its sa‘ and mudd, and transfer its fever to Mahya‘ah, which is al-Juhfah.”
H-9898-141-prep-2:p1: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered the mosque while the people, overcome by the fever, were praying seated. The Prophet ﷺ said: “The prayer of one who prays seated is half the prayer of one who prays standing.” The people then completed the prayer standing. The Prophet ﷺ then said: “O Allah, grant Madinah twice the blessing You granted Makkah!”
sp_caveverse_baghawi_sakina:p2: “So Allah sent down His tranquility upon him.”
sp_caveverse_baghawi_sakina:p3: It was said: Upon the Prophet ﷺ. Ibn ‘Abbas said: Upon Abu Bakr, for the Prophet ﷺ had already been granted tranquility before that.
sp_caveverse_baghawi_sakina:p4: “And He strengthened him with forces you did not see.”
sp_caveverse_baghawi_sakina:p6: They were the angels. They descended, turning the faces and eyes of the disbelievers away from seeing him. It was also said: They cast terror into the hearts of the disbelievers until they turned back.
sp_caveverse_sakina_ibn_abbas:p2: “So Allah sent down His tranquility upon him.”
sp_caveverse_sakina_ibn_abbas:p3: He said: “Upon Abu Bakr, because tranquility had never ceased to be with the Prophet ﷺ.”
sp_earlier_exp_h_1681_5922_hs_billeting_: “‘Uthman ibn Maz‘un was allotted a place to stay with them when the Ansar drew lots to house the emigrants. Umm al-‘Ala’ said: ‘‘Uthman fell ill in our home, and I cared for him until he died. We wrapped him in his clothes. The Prophet ﷺ came to us, and I said, “May Allah have mercy on you, Abu al-Sa’ib. I bear witness for you that Allah has honored you.” The Prophet ﷺ said, “How do you know that Allah has honored him?” I said, “I do not know—may my father and mother be sacrificed for you, Messenger of Allah. Who, then?” He said, “As for him, certainty has come to him. By Allah, I hope for good for him. But by Allah, I do not know what will be done with me, though I am the Messenger of Allah.” She said: “By Allah, after that I will not declare anyone’s virtue.” She said: “That saddened me, and I fell asleep. Then I was shown a flowing spring belonging to ‘Uthman ibn Maz‘un. I went to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and told him, and he said, ‘That is his deed.’””
sp_earlier_exp_h_23833_493_prep_cont:p2: She said: “By Allah, I know of no household in Islam that suffered what the family of Abu Salamah suffered. And I have never seen a companion more noble than ‘Uthman ibn Talhah.”
sp_earlier_exp_h_23833_493_prep_foot_3:p:
‘Uthman was still a disbeliever on the day he migrated with Umm Salamah. He became Muslim only during the Hudaybiyyah truce, and migrated before the conquest with Khalid ibn al-Walid. His brothers, Musafi‘, Kilab, and al-Harith, and their father were killed on the day of Uhud. His uncle, ‘Uthman ibn Abi Talhah, was also killed as a disbeliever on the day of Uhud; the keys to the Ka‘bah were in his possession. In the year of the conquest, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ entrusted them to ‘Uthman ibn Talhah ibn Abi Talhah and his uncle, Shaybah ibn ‘Uthman ibn Abi Talhah. He is the ancestor of the Banu Shaybah, the custodians of the Ka‘bah.

The name of their ancestor, Abu Talhah, was ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Abd al-‘Uzza. ‘Uthman, may Allah be pleased with him, was martyred at Ajnadayn at the beginning of ‘Umar’s caliphate.
sp_earlier_exp_h_23833_494_prep_cont:p1: Ibn ‘Uthman, on the day at al-Radm, as they were climbing toward the upper part of Makkah. ‘Utbah ibn Rabi‘ah saw its doors flapping, with the house empty and no one living in it. When he saw it in that state, he sighed deeply, then said:
sp_earlier_exp_h_23833_494_prep_cont:p2: Every home, no matter how long it remains secure, will one day be overtaken by misfortune and grief.
sp_earlier_exp_h_23833_494_prep_cont:p3: Ibn Hisham said: This verse is by Abu Du’ad al-Iyadi, from one of his poems. Al-hub means anguish; in another context it means need, and it is also said to mean sin.
sp_earlier_exp_h_23833_494_prep_cont:p4: Ibn Ishaq said: Then ‘Utbah ibn Rabi‘ah said: “The home of Banu Jahsh has become empty of its people!” Abu Jahl said: “Why are you grieving for such a worthless nobody?”
sp_earlier_exp_h_23833_494_prep_cont:p5: Ibn Hisham said: Al-qull means “the individual.” Labid ibn Rabi‘ah said:
sp_earlier_exp_h_23833_494_prep_cont:p6: Every freeborn son’s end is ... say: even if the numbers grow greater.
sp_earlier_exp_h_23833_494_prep_cont:p7: Ibn Ishaq said: Then he said, “This is the work of my nephew. He has divided our community, scattered our affairs, and severed our ties.” The household of Abu Salamah ibn ‘Abd al-Asad and ‘Amir ibn Rabi‘ah was
sp_earlier_exp_h_23833_495_prep_cont:p1: ‘Abdullah ibn Jahsh and his brother Abu Ahmad ibn Jahsh stayed with Mubashshir ibn ‘Abd al-Mundhir ibn Zanbar at Quba, among Banu ‘Amr ibn ‘Awf. Then the emigrants arrived in groups. Banu Ghanm ibn Dudan were Muslims, and all their men and women had emigrated to Madinah with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: ‘Abdullah ibn Jahsh, his brother Abu Ahmad ibn Jahsh, ‘Ukkashah ibn Mihsan, Shuja‘ and ‘Uqbah, the sons of Wahb, and Arbad ibn Humayrah.
sp_earlier_exp_h_23833_498_prep_787:p1: Ibn Ishaq said: Nafi‘ related to me, from ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar, from ‘Umar, in his account. He said:
sp_earlier_exp_h_23833_498_prep_787:p2:
We used to say, “Allah will accept from one who has been put to trial neither a ransom, nor compensation, nor repentance: people who knew Allah, then returned to disbelief because of a trial that befell them!” He said: They used to say this about themselves.
When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ arrived in Madinah, Allah Most High revealed concerning them, and concerning what we and they had said about themselves:
sp_earlier_exp_h_23833_498_prep_787:p3: Say, “O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of Allah’s mercy. Indeed, Allah forgives all sins. He is truly the All-Forgiving, the Most Merciful. Turn back to your Lord and submit to Him before the punishment comes upon you,”
sp_earlier_exp_h_23833_499_prep_788:p1: Ibn Hisham said: Someone I trust told me:
sp_earlier_exp_h_23833_499_prep_788:p2: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said while he was in Madinah, “Who will bring me ‘Ayyash ibn Abi Rabi‘ah and Hisham ibn al-‘As?” Al-Walid ibn al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah said, “I will bring them to you, Messenger of Allah.” He set out for Makkah and arrived there in secret. He met a woman carrying food and said to her, “Where are you going, servant of Allah?” She said, “I am going to these two prisoners”—meaning them. He followed her until he learned where they were. They were imprisoned in a house with no roof. When evening came, he climbed over the wall to them, then took a piece of stone and placed it beneath their shackles. He struck the shackles with his sword and cut through them. His sword was therefore called “The Stone.” Then he put them on his camel and rode off with them. He stumbled, and his toe bled, so he said:
sp_earlier_exp_h_23833_499_prep_788:p3:
“You are only a toe that has bled;
what you have suffered is in Allah’s cause.”
sp_earlier_exp_h_23833_499_prep_788:p4: Then he brought them to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in Madinah.
sp_earlier_exp_h_23833_499_prep_cont:p1: “then you will not be helped. Follow the best of what has been sent down to you from your Lord before the punishment comes upon you suddenly, while you are unaware.”
sp_earlier_exp_h_23833_499_prep_cont:p3: ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab said: “So I wrote it with my own hand on a sheet and sent it to Hisham ibn al-‘As.”
sp_earlier_exp_h_23833_499_prep_cont:p4: He said: Hisham ibn al-‘As said: “When it reached me, I began reading it at Dhu Tuwa, going up and down with it, but I could not understand it, until I said, ‘O Allah, make me understand it.’ Then Allah, Exalted is He, cast into my heart that it had been sent down concerning us, and concerning what we used to say about ourselves and what was said about us.” He said: “So I returned to my camel, mounted it, and caught up with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in Madinah.”
sp_earlier_exp_h_23833_502_prep_794:p1: ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn ‘Awf and a group of the Emigrants stayed with Sa‘d ibn al-Rabi‘, the brother of Banu al-Harith ibn al-Khazraj, in the home of Banu al-Harith ibn al-Khazraj.
sp_earlier_exp_h_23833_502_prep_796:p1: Muṣ‘ab ibn ‘Umayr ibn Hāshim, brother of Banū ‘Abd al-Dār, stayed with Sa‘d ibn Mu‘ādh ibn al-Nu‘mān, brother of Banū ‘Abd al-Ashhal, in the home of Banū ‘Abd al-Ashhal.
sp_earlier_exp_h_23833_502_prep_798:p1: ‘Uthmān ibn ‘Affān stayed with Aws ibn Thābit ibn al-Mundhir, brother of Hassān ibn Thābit, in the home of Banū al-Najjār. For that reason, Hassān loved ‘Uthmān and wept for him when he was killed.
sp_earlier_exp_h_7478_982_ra_musa_early::
As for Talhah, he went out to Syria.

Then the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ followed one after another to Madinah in groups. Some of his Companions remained in Makkah until they arrived in Madinah after his arrival there. Among them was Sa‘d ibn Abi Waqqas.
sp_earlier_exp_h_7478_983_ra_umar_hisham: Say, “O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of Allah’s mercy.”

‘Umar said: “So I wrote it down by hand, then sent it to Hisham.” Hisham ibn al-‘As said: “When it reached me, I went out with it to Dhu Tuwa and kept going up and down with it, trying to understand it. I said, ‘O Allah, make me understand it.’ Then I realized that it had been revealed concerning us, just as we used to say to ourselves—or, as it is said, concerning us. I returned, mounted my camel, and caught up with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.”
sp_earlier_exp_h_930_744_prep_saad_date::
Muslim also narrated it in his Sahih, through Isra’il, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Bara’ ibn ‘Azib, with a similar wording.
It explicitly states that Sa‘d ibn Abi Waqqas emigrated before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ arrived in Madinah. Musa ibn ‘Uqbah, reporting from al-Zuhri, claimed that he emigrated only after the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, but the correct view is what was stated earlier.
sp_earlier_exp_h_9783_994_early_migrants:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ instructed his Companions who were with him in Makkah, among the Muslims, to emigrate and set out for Madinah, and to join their brothers among the Ansar. [He said: “Allah ﷿ has given you brothers and a home where you will be safe.”] So they left in succession. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ remained in Makkah, waiting for his Lord to permit him to leave Makkah. The first of the Messenger of Allah’s ﷺ Companions from Quraysh, and then from Banu Makhzum, to emigrate to Madinah was Abu Salamah ibn ‘Abd al-Asad ibn Hilal ibn ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar ibn Makhzum. He emigrated to Madinah a year before the pledge of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ’s Companions at al-‘Aqabah. He had come to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in Makkah from the land of Abyssinia. When Quraysh persecuted him, and news reached him that some of the Ansar had become Muslims, he set out for Madinah as an emigrant.

The first emigrant to arrive in Madinah after Abu Salamah was ‘Amir ibn Rabi‘ah, an ally of Banu ‘Adi ibn Ka‘b. His wife, Layla bint Abi Hathmah ibn Ghanim ibn ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Awf ibn ‘Ubayd ibn ‘Uwayj ibn ‘Adi ibn Ka‘b, was with him. Then came ‘Abdullah ibn Jahsh ibn Ri’ab and Abu Ahmad ibn Jahsh, who was blind and used to walk through the upper and lower parts of Makkah without a guide. Then the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ followed one another to Madinah.

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ remained in Makkah after his Companions among the emigrants, waiting for permission to emigrate. None of the emigrants remained behind with him in Makkah without being seized and imprisoned or persecuted, except ‘Ali ibn Abi Talib and Abu Bakr ibn Abi Quhafah. Abu Bakr often asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for permission to emigrate, [but the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would say to him: “Do not be hasty; perhaps Allah will provide you with a companion.”] Abu Bakr hoped that he would be that companion.
sp_earlier_exp_h_9862_213_ishaq_early_ab: He was the Prophet’s ﷺ cousin, and the first to emigrate with his wife to Abyssinia and then to Madinah. His wife was Umm Salamah, whom he had taken with him. When he died, the Prophet ﷺ married her afterward.
sp_guide_hajar_age_end:p1: Among those who emigrated, Abu Bakr was the only one with gray hair. His statement, “The Prophet of Allah was a young man, not known to be [older],” apparently means that Abu Bakr was older than the Prophet ﷺ, but that is not so.
sp_guide_hajar_age_end:p4: I say: He was as he supposed, but this is known only of al-‘Abbas. As for Abu Bakr, it is established in Sahih Muslim, from Mu‘awiyah, that he lived for sixty-three years. He lived for two years and some months after the Prophet ﷺ, so, according to the soundest view of Abu Bakr’s age, he must have been more than two years younger than the Prophet ﷺ.
sp_guide_hajar_age_start:p1: His saying, “Abu Bakr was an old man,” means that his hair had turned gray. The statement that he “was recognized” means that he used to pass through Madinah on trading journeys. The Prophet ﷺ differed from him in both respects: he had not traveled from Makkah for a long time, and his hair had not turned gray. In reality, however, he ﷺ was older than Abu Bakr. A report from Anas will appear in this chapter.
sp_permission_h_23833_491_prep_778:p1: Ibn Ishaq said: When Allah Most High gave him ﷺ permission to fight, and this group of the Ansar pledged allegiance to him to follow Islam and support him and those who followed him, and Muslims found refuge with them, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ instructed his Companions from among the emigrants of his people, and the Muslims with him in Makkah, to leave for Madinah, migrate there, and join their brothers among the Ansar. He said, “Allah ﷿ has given you brothers and a home where you will be safe.” So they left in successive groups, while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ remained in Makkah, waiting for his Lord to give him permission to leave Makkah and migrate to Madinah.
sp_permission_h_23833_503_800:p1: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ remained in Makkah after his Companions from among the emigrants, waiting for permission to migrate. None of the emigrants remained behind with him in Makkah except those who had been detained or persecuted, as well as ‘Ali ibn Abi Talib and Abu Bakr ibn Abi Quhafah al-Siddiq ﵄. Abu Bakr would often ask the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for permission to migrate, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would say to him, “Do not hurry; perhaps Allah will provide you with a companion.” Abu Bakr hoped that he would be that companion.
sp_quba_chapter_10:p4_cont: He said, and Anas said: “It was as I have told you: there were the graves of polytheists there, there were ruins there, and there were palm trees there. So the Messenger of Allah ordered…”
sp_quba_chapter_12:p9_hajar: The distinction may have been due to the fact that he ﷺ stayed for a long time at the mosque in Madinah, whereas he stayed at the mosque of Quba for only a few days. This distinction is sufficient, without the need for what al-Qurtubi proposed. The truth is that both were founded on piety. As for the rest of the verse, Allah Most High says:
sp_quba_chapter_12:p9_qurtubi: Al-Qurtubi said: “This question came from someone who saw the two mosques as equal, since both had been built by the Prophet ﷺ. That is why the Prophet ﷺ was asked about it, and he answered that what was meant was his mosque. The distinction that led to his mosque being specified rather than the mosque of Quba may have been that the mosque of Quba was not built at Allah’s firm command to His Prophet, or that it was based on an opinion he had formed, unlike his own mosque; or perhaps he or his Companions experienced in it spiritual states that they did not experience elsewhere.” End quote.
sp_thawr_exp_h_146_241_support_and_guide: The account returns to the beginning. They said: Abu Bakr had a flock of sheep given to him as a gift, which ‘Amir ibn Fuhayrah tended. He would bring them to them at night, and they would milk them. At daybreak, he would take them out to graze with the people.

‘Aishah said: “We prepared provisions for the two of them as well as we could, and packed food for them in a leather bag. Asma’ bint Abu Bakr cut a strip from her waistband and tied the bag with it. She cut another strip and made it a tie for the mouth of the waterskin. For this reason she was called ‘the woman of the two waistbands.’”

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ and Abu Bakr stayed in the cave for three nights. ‘Abdullah ibn Abu Bakr would spend the night with them. Abu Bakr hired a man from Banu al-Dayl, a skilled guide, named ‘Abdullah ibn Urayqit, who followed the religion of unbelief. But the two of them trusted him. They set out, accompanied by ‘Amir ibn Fuhayrah, and Ibn Urayqit led them along a coastal route. Quraysh had no idea where the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had gone.

Until they heard the voice of a jinn from below Makkah, though he could not be seen:
“May Allah, Lord of the people, reward with the best reward … two companions who stayed at the tent of Umm Ma‘bad.
They came down with goodness and departed with it … whoever spends the evening as Muhammad’s companion has indeed prospered.”
sp_thawr_exp_h_23833_508_807:p2: Abu Bakr instructed his son, ‘Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr, to listen during the day to what people were saying about the two of them, then to come to them at dusk with whatever news there was that day.
sp_thawr_exp_h_23833_508_807:p3: He instructed his freedman, ‘Amir ibn Fuhayrah, to graze his sheep during the day, then bring them to rest with the two of them, coming to them at dusk in the cave.
sp_thawr_exp_h_23833_508_807:p4: When evening came, Asma’ bint Abi Bakr would bring them whatever food they needed.
sp_thawr_exp_h_23833_509_808:p1: Ibn Ishaq said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ remained in the cave for three nights, with Abu Bakr. When Quraysh lost him, they offered a hundred camels to anyone who brought him back to them.
sp_thawr_exp_h_23833_509_808:p2: During the day, ‘Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr would be among Quraysh, listening to what they planned and what they said about the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and Abu Bakr. Then, when evening came, he would go to them and tell them the news.
sp_thawr_exp_h_23833_509_808:p3: ‘Amir ibn Fuhayrah, Abu Bakr’s freedman, would graze among the shepherds of the people of Makkah. When evening came, he would bring Abu Bakr’s sheep to them. They would milk them and slaughter one. When ‘Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr set out from them for Makkah in the morning, ‘Amir ibn Fuhayrah would follow his tracks with the sheep until he erased them.
sp_thawr_exp_h_23833_509_808:p4: When the three days had passed and the people had ceased searching for them, the man they had hired came to them with their two camels and a camel of his own. Asma’ bint Abi Bakr brought them their provisions, but she had forgotten to bring a cord for tying them. When they set out, she went to fasten the provisions, but found she had no cord. So she untied her waist belt, used it as a cord, and tied the provisions with it.
sp_thawr_exp_h_41_1252_cave_explanation:: “When the two of them were in the cave”
It is a crevice in Mount Thawr in Makkah.
sp_thawr_exp_h_43_7827_three_nights:p1: 16730— Ibn Waki‘ narrated to us; he said: My father narrated to us, from Sharik, from Ibrahim ibn Muhajir, from Mujahid, who said:
sp_thawr_exp_h_43_7827_three_nights:p2: Abu Bakr stayed with the Prophet ﷺ in the cave for three nights.
sp_thawr_exp_h_43_7827_three_nights:p3: 16731— Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-A‘la narrated to us; he said: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma‘mar, from al-Zuhri:
sp_thawr_exp_h_43_7827_three_nights:p4: “When the two of them were in the cave,”
sp_thawr_exp_h_43_7827_three_nights:p5: he said: In the mountain called Thawr, where the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and Abu Bakr stayed for three nights.
sp_thawr_exp_h_7478_1001_ra_urwa_musa_ca: He would stay in Makkah, and every night ‘Amir ibn Fuhayrah would bring the sheep to them. They would milk them and set out in the latter part of the night. Then, in the morning, he would take the sheep out to pasture and be among the people’s shepherds, so no one would notice him. When the voices had quieted around them and it was known that they were no longer being pursued, their companion came to them with their two camels. They had remained in the cave for two days and two nights.
In the narration of Musa ibn ‘Uqbah: three nights.

Then the two set out, taking ‘Amir ibn Fuhayrah with them to serve and assist them. Abu Bakr let him ride behind him and took turns with him on his mount. No one accompanied them except ‘Amir ibn Fuhayrah and a guide from Banu ‘Adi. The guide led them along the road and took them through the lower part of Makkah. Then he went with them along the coast, south of ‘Usfan, and continued until he joined the main road after taking them past Qudayd.”
sp_thawr_exp_h_7478_999_ra_urwa_musa_cav: “They rode out in every direction seeking the Prophet ﷺ and sent word to the people at the watering places, ordering them to help and promising them a great reward. They came to Mount Thawr, where the cave in which the Prophet ﷺ was staying lay, and climbed up until they reached its top. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ and Abu Bakr heard their voices. Abu Bakr became alarmed, and worry and fear overcame him. At that, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him, ‘Do not grieve; Allah is with us.’ The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed, and tranquility from Allah descended upon him.”
“Then Allah sent down His tranquility upon His Messenger and upon the believers,”
“and made the word of those who disbelieved the lowest, while the word of Allah is supreme. Allah is Almighty, All-Wise.”
sp_thawr_exp_h_9898_124_prep_2:p2: The polytheists set out in pursuit of the two of them. They came to the mountain and looked down toward the cave.
sp_thawr_exp_h_9898_124_prep_2:p3: Abu Bakr said, “Messenger of Allah, if one of them were to look beneath his feet, he would see us.” The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, “Abu Bakr, what do you think of two when Allah is the third of them?”
sp_thawr_exp_h_9898_124_prep_2:p4: Allah blinded their eyes to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. When they had given up hope, they turned back.
sp_umm_mabad_gloss:p12: Her words, “No paunch made him seem unattractive,” mean that he did not have a large belly.
sp_umm_mabad_gloss:p14: Her words, “A small head did not make him seem unattractive,” refer to a small head; a man is called small-headed. Her words, “handsome and well-proportioned,” both mean handsome. He said: The poet praised a people, saying:
sp_umm_mabad_gloss:p17: As though dinars lay upon their features … even though the encounter had worn their faces thin.
sp_umm_mabad_gloss:p18: He means: Even if the encounter with war has worn them down, their beauty remains unchanged. By “features,” he means handsome faces. Her words, “His eyes were intensely black,” refer to the blackness of the iris; a man is called intensely black-eyed, and a woman intensely black-eyed. Her words, “His eyelashes were curved”: Some people thought the word meant curved, but I think it means long and flowing, as does anything elongated and hanging freely. A cloud hanging low over the earth is also described as long and flowing. Her words, “There was a slight huskiness in his voice”: it was slightly hoarse, resembling a mild roughness, but not severe; rather, it was pleasant. Gazelles are described this way. Her words, “His neck was long”: this means tall; a man is called long-necked and a woman long-necked, and this is considered praiseworthy in people. Her word “arched-browed” means that his eyebrows were curved. “Joined-browed” means that his eyebrows met between his eyes.
sp_umm_mabad_gloss:p22: And her words, “attended to and surrounded”: “attended to” means served. Allah, exalted is He, said:
sp_umm_mabad_gloss:p25: “Surrounded” means that his companions gathered around him, closed in around him, and encircled him.
sp_umm_mabad_gloss:p3: Abu ‘Ubayd said: When someone says, “Yā so-and-so,” with the alif pronounced with a fatḥah, it is a plea for help; and “Yā”
sp_umm_mabad_gloss:p5: …the Muslims. When expressing wonder or calling out, one says, “Yā so-and-so,” with a kasrah. His phrase “the rear of the tent” means its back part; there are two forms of the word, kisar and kasar. Some said that al-kisar is the front of the tent. His phrase “so she spread her legs apart before him” means that she parted her legs, as a woman does when being milked. His phrase “in a vessel that would satisfy the group” means it would keep them from being overcome by thirst, because there was enough for them to drink. His phrase “he milked into it in a copious stream” means a flow; the word is used for every kind of flow. The same word occurs when he ﷺ was asked about Hajj and said:
sp_umm_mabad_gloss:p7: “Al-‘ajj” means raising the voice in the talbiyah, and “ath-thajj” means the flowing of the sacrificial animals’ blood. His words “arāḍū” originally refer to pouring milk onto milk. Her words “arāḍū” mean drinking milk that was poured onto other milk. His words “then he left it with her” mean that he left it behind. His words “driving goats that walked weakly from emaciation”: “tasāwuk” means walking feebly. His words “the sheep are ‘āzib” mean that they had gone away from the house and out to pasture. “Al-ḥiyyal” means those that are not pregnant.
sp_umm_mabad_gloss:p8: Her description of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, “radiant in appearance,” means handsome; “radiant” means handsome. “Bright-faced” describes a face with light and radiance; a man may be described as bright-faced or radiant. Al-A‘sha said:
sp_umm_mabad_ibn_kathir:p1: As he passed by, he came to Umm Ma‘bad, daughter of Ka‘b, of Banu Ka‘b ibn Khuza‘ah. This is what Ibn Hisham said. Yunus, reporting from Ibn Ishaq, said: Her name was ‘Atikah, daughter of Khalid ibn Munqidh ibn Rabi‘ah ibn Asram. Al-Um awi said: She was ‘Atikah, daughter of Tabee‘, an ally of Banu Munqidh ibn Rabi‘ah ibn Asram ibn Dhabis ibn Haram ibn Hubshiyyah ibn Ka‘b ibn ‘Amr. Her children were Ma‘bad, Nadrah, and Hunaidah, the children of Abu Ma‘bad, whose name was Aktham ibn ‘Abd al-‘Uzza ibn Munqidh ibn Rabi‘ah ibn Asram ibn Dhabis.
sp_umm_mabad_story:p20: By morning, a loud voice was heard in Makkah, but they could not tell who was speaking:
sp_umm_mabad_story:p23:
May the Lord of all people reward with the finest reward
Two companions who stopped at the tent of Umm Ma‘bad.
They came to her with guidance, and she found guidance through them;
Fortunate is the one who became Muhammad’s companion.
O people of Qusayy, what a noble deed Allah granted them,
A deed whose distinction cannot be repaid!
May the place of your young woman bring joy to the Banu Ka‘b,
And may her seat lie in wait for the believers.
Ask your sister about her sheep and her vessel;
If you ask the sheep, it will bear witness.
He called for a barren ewe, and it yielded milk for him,
Pure, with foam rising on the ewe’s udder.
He left it with her as a pledge for a milker,
Who would take it back and forth between the watering place and the spring.
sp_umm_mabad_story:p25: And in the narration of Abu ‘Amr ibn Hamdan:
sp_umm_mabad_story:p26: By morning, a voice was heard in Madinah, between heaven and earth. They heard it but could not see who was speaking.
sp_umm_mabad_story:p30: When Hassan ibn Thabit al-Ansari heard the caller, he sprang up, answering the caller and saying:
